hints.title: All-Ones Subgrid Dimension Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the largest square containing only '1's requires verifying all three neighboring quarters. How can determining the maximum square cornered at each cell derive from its top, left, and diagonal predecessors?

hints.title: Triplet Minimum Side Extension Invariant
hints.text: If matrix[r][c] is '1', the maximum side length ending at (r, c) is 1 plus the minimum of side lengths ending at (r - 1, c), (r, c - 1), and (r - 1, c - 1).

hints.title: 1D Array Rolling Square Update Procedure
hints.text: Maintain a 1D array of width n + 1 and a variable tracking the top-left diagonal value. For each cell with value '1', update its entry to 1 plus the minimum of its left neighbor, previous row neighbor, and the diagonal predecessor, maintaining the maximum side length seen. Return the squared maximum side.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Single scan over M x N cells updating a 1D buffer of size N + 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking every possible square from each cell takes O((M * N)^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Compressing 2D grid table to 1D row takes O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that 1 + min(top, left, top-left) calculates the largest square side.
